steps.why: The question asks why, so the answer must rest on the law that connects diffusion rate to molar mass, with the three molar masses written down for comparison.
common_mistakes: Naming CH₄ with no reason. The why carries one full mark.
Comparing the sizes of the molecules instead of their molar masses.
steps.margin_note: The three molar masses on one line are the evidence the examiner looks for.

steps.label: The fastest gas

lines.text: CH₄ diffuses fastest, because its molar mass (16 g mol⁻¹) is the lowest

lines: The lowest molar mass gives the highest rate,
steps.why: Among 28, 32 and 16 g mol⁻¹, the smallest molar mass belongs to CH₄, and the law says the smallest molar mass diffuses at the highest rate.
common_mistakes: Picking O₂ because it is the heaviest. The heaviest gas diffuses slowest, not fastest.
steps.memory_tip: Methane is the lightest of the three, so it is the fastest.
steps.margin_note: Box the gas and its molar mass together.

insider_note: Write the three molar masses before naming CH₄ — the comparison is the reason the question asks for.
